reasons.specificity: Strongly source-specific: it distinguishes imperialism, tax-farming, patrimonialism, estates, responsibility, and edition substitutions, and preserves coauthorship and Riley’s labelled adaptations. The pair table covers all 28 candidate IDs, though some are grouped.
reasons.anchoring: Most settled rows quote genuine, relevant passages. However RW0011 is wrongly called unverifiable even though the supplied Riley passage quotes “not ‘absolute contrasts, but rather supplements’” and the supplied Weber p.127 contains the same words. RW0050, RW0076, and RW0084 are likewise directly anchored but arbitrarily excluded from settled findings.
reasons.non_obviousness: Useful distinctions include A180 versus MWG printed p.180, imperialist-profit comparison versus a declining-profit thesis, historical tax-farming versus M–A–M′, and estate/class overlap without identity. It also correctly separates Weber’s examples from Riley’s contemporary applications.
reasons.coherence: The headline says 11 settled and 17 unresolved, but the audit itself judges RW0050, RW0076, and RW0084 accurate, while RW0011 is textually settled by the supplied packet. Calling these unreconciled because no “final retained row” exists is an internal workflow artifact, not an evidentiary distinction. The enormous malformed scope appendix also conflicts with the completed audit above.
reasons.usefulness: The main paired table, thematic synthesis, edition notes, counts, and bounded practice conclusion are useful with the texts open. Usefulness is reduced by incorrect unresolved classifications, grouped unresolved entries in the summary table, and a very long repetitive scope-assessment appendix that obscures the actual audit.
reasons.hallucination_risk: The analysis is generally cautious about packet limits and avoids global absence claims. Risk remains material because it converts several demonstrably anchored pairs into unresolved ones and overstates RW0088 as accurate: Weber pp.965–66 describe farming out collection, stipulated remittances, and the capitalist farmer, but do not state Riley and Brenner’s specific claim that entrepreneurs advanced money to the sovereign before receiving the right.

decisive_errors.claim: RW0011 is “Unverifiable at the indexed locus” and belongs among the 17 unresolved pairs.
decisive_errors.counter_passage: Riley quotes: “An ethic of conviction and an ethic of responsibility were not ‘absolute contrasts, but rather supplements’” (Tony Judt, p.47). Weber states: “an ethic of ultimate ends and an ethic of responsibility are not absolute contrasts but rather supplements” (From Max Weber, p.127). The supplied packet therefore settles textual fidelity, with only an impression note remaining.

decisive_errors.claim: Only 11 pairs are settled; RW0050, RW0076, and RW0084 are excluded because no “reconciled final pair row was retained.”
decisive_errors.counter_passage: RW0050 is supported by Weber’s exact query “What shall we do, and, how shall we arrange our lives?” (pp.152–53); RW0076 by the exact power definition at E&S p.53; RW0084 by Weber’s statement that domination normally cultivates belief in legitimacy at E&S pp.212–14. Missing internal retention is not source-based unresolvedness.

decisive_errors.claim: RW0088 is an accurate attribution of entrepreneurs “advancing money to the sovereign in exchange for the right to collect taxes.”
decisive_errors.counter_passage: E&S pp.965–66 says public tax collection was farmed out, the official might hand over a stipulated amount and retain the surplus, and the tax-farmer was a private capitalist. It does not explicitly describe an advance payment to purchase the collection right; that narrower mechanism should be marked fair/selective or only partly verified.

score.one_line: A highly specific and often insightful audit undermined by an internally inconsistent settled/unresolved count, several false unverifiable verdicts despite exact packet anchors, and a burdensome malformed scope appendix.
